text.p: Norwood Promotional Products Inc on Tuesday said it planned a sweeping restructuring and that it expects an after tax cost of $2.9 million.
Norwood said it would close the retail division of its Alpha Products company and that it is holding discussions with interested parties regarding the sale of the Alpha retail business and assets.
As a result, the promotional products division of Alpha Products will be relocated to the existing Radio Cap Co division facilities in San Antonio and Pittsburgh.
Expenses to dispose of the operations and valuation adjustments of assets are estimated to be about $2.9 million after-tax.

Norwood said for the fourth quarter of 1997, the company estimates that net income, excluding Alpha Retail, restructuring charges and other one-time charges, will be in the range of $0.25 to $0.30 per share, compared to $0.20 per share for the fourth quarter of 1996. The combined after-tax impact on net income of Alpha Retail, restructuring charges and other one-time charges for the fourth quarter is estimated to be about $4.7 million, or $0.91 per share.

For fiscal 1997, the company estimates that net income, excluding Alpha Retail, restructuring charges and other one-time charges, will be in the range of $1.30 to $1.35 per share, compared to $1.01 per share for same period last year.
The combined after-tax impact on net income of Alpha Retail, restructuring charges and other one-time charges for fiscal 1997 is estimated to be approximately $6.2 million, or $1.13.

Norwood said as a result of last week's announcement that Frank Krasovec, chairman, president and chief executive officer, has assumed day to day control, following the resignation of Robert P. Whitesell as president and chief operating officer the San Antonio corporate office will be closed, with the operations moving to the Austin executive office.

In a separate transaction, the Key Industries division (Econoline and California Line) will be realigned with the Barlow Group division, which will enable the company to capitalize on processing capacity and product line restructuring. In connection with these initiatives, the Company estimates incurring a one-time charge of approximately $500,000 after-tax.

Norwood also said it will recognize a roughly $475,000 after tax charge in relation to last weeks announcement that the letter of intent and all negotiations related to the acquisition of the Rou bill Group have been terminated.

Norwood also said it to close a new $125 million Senior Secured Credit Facility provided by Merrill Lynch & Co. The company said it will recognize about $230,000 after-tax, of unamortized debt financing costs on the existing facility.
